findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated: abstract methods not implemented
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with a bare `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented. Because MetricAlertFire.detector_handler is set to this class and `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, any Detector row whose `type` slug resolves to `metric_alert_fire` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` inside process_detectors, and the exception is not caught anywhere in that path. The old code returned a working (if stubbed) DetectorHandler; the new code turns a previously-valid detector type into an unhandled crash. Either implement the abstract members or don't register the class as a detector_handler yet.

findings.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with the wrong group key
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected occurrence/event_data are built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is then called with group key `"group_key"`. The handler's `build_occurrence_and_event_data` will therefore produce an occurrence whose fingerprint is `"<detector_id>:group_key"`, while the expected occurrence's fingerprint is `"<detector_id>:val1"` (the fingerprint is derived from the group key in `build_mock_occurrence_and_event`). Unless IssueOccurrence equality is trivially true, this assertion fails; if it does pass, it means occurrence equality is not actually being verified, so the test asserts nothing meaningful about the produced occurrence. The expected occurrence should be built with `"group_key"` to match the group key being evaluated.

findings.title: Unguarded cross-enum conversion PriorityLevel(new_status) from DetectorPriorityLevel
findings.body: `evaluate_group_key_value` converts the internal `DetectorPriorityLevel` to the issue `PriorityLevel` via `PriorityLevel(new_status)`, relying on the two unrelated enums having identical integer values. If `DetectorPriorityLevel` ever gains or changes a value that has no `PriorityLevel` counterpart, this raises an uncaught `ValueError` at evaluation time, breaking the detector. Consider an explicit mapping between the two enums (or guarding the conversion) so the failure mode is intentional rather than incidental.

findings.title: Stale docstring: evaluate still documented as returning a list
findings.body: The docstring on `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the signature and implementation were changed in this PR to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. The docstring should be updated so callers reading it aren't misled about the return type and the duplicate-group-key dedupe semantics.

findings.title: Tests never verify the value passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data; wrong value used in multi-group test
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` argument entirely, so no test asserts that the correct group value is forwarded to the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook. This is evidenced by `test_state_results_multi_group`, which builds the expected occurrence for group_2 with `value=6` even though the data packet contains `{"group_2": 10}` — the test passes only because the builder discards the value. If a real handler includes the value in evidence/subtitle, this gap would hide a wrong-value bug. The mock builder should incorporate `value` (e.g. into `evidence_data` or `subtitle`) so the forwarded value is actually asserted.
